A high-performance, deterministic quality, safety, and verification plugin for **OpenCode** AI coding agents.

OpenCode Guardian continuously supervises agent turns: guiding model execution before calls, correlating tool results at session idle, intercepting recognized destructive shell actions and secret-bearing file writes, redacting sensitive tool outputs before model visibility, and requiring verifiable tool evidence before agents declare tasks complete.

---

## 📊 Verification & Live Acceptance

![Automated and host acceptance results](docs/assets/verification-overview.svg)

> Guardian **v0.16.1** was verified on **22 November 2026** against live **OpenCode v2.3.2** on Node **26.13.1** and Bun **1.4.4**.

- **Current Automated Verification:** **791 / 791** unit, security, mesh interoperability, project scope isolation, toast notification, and regression tests passing.
- **Sandbox Scenarios:** **18 / 18** end-to-end multi-turn agent failure and recovery scenarios verified.
- **Live V2 Host Acceptance:** **10 / 10** real-host checks verified (packed `.tgz` in Node 26.13.1 + Bun 1.4.4, full V2.3.2 server hooks + `./rpc` + TUI slots/commands, and live `opencode v2.3.2` CLI host).
- **Static Analysis:** standard and strict TypeScript gates pass (`--strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes`); Oxlint reports **0 warnings / 0 errors** across 112 files.
- **Low-I/O & Zero-Pollution Telemetry Architecture:** Default `violations` mode eliminates 90–95% of disk syscalls, caching directory verification, bounding logs to 512 KiB, and isolating per-project audit logs in `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` without polluting project `.opencode/` directories.

Read the comprehensive [V2 Acceptance Report](docs/acceptance-v2.md) and [Verification and Acceptance Report](docs/verification-report.md) for reproduction steps, methodology, and full test matrices.

See the [0.16.1 release notes](CHANGELOG.md) for TUI conversation banner auto-expiry/prompt-clear/click-to-dismiss fixes, Universal OpenCode V2 Plugin Mesh Bridge (`src/bridge.ts` v2.2.0), N-way `opencode-hi` & `opencode-smart-questions` coordination, external per-project state isolation, and local-vs-global scope boundaries.

## ✨ Key Highlights

- **Pure OpenCode V2 Architecture:** Built natively for **OpenCode V2** (`@opencode/plugin >=2.3.0`) with dedicated `.` (server), `./tui` (OpenTUI/Solid), and `./rpc` (typed intervention RPC) exports.
- **Compact TUI Sidebar & Auto-Expiring Conversation Banner:** A compact two-column status widget (`sidebar.content`) that expands to show Guardian diagnostics with a single click, paired with an inline conversation banner (`session.composer.top`) that auto-expires after its toast TTL (`4s` warnings / `5s` errors), clears immediately on new user prompts, and supports click-to-dismiss.
- **In-App Update Indicator:** Shows a green `(↑)` header icon and places `Update available` first in the sidebar when npm reports a newer release.
- **Guardian Commands:** Ctrl+P and slash commands display detailed status, activity, diagnostics, rules, configuration and version; confirmed statistics reset preserves audit history.
- **Isolated Per-Project Audit Log (Zero Repository Pollution):** Stores safe event codes, reasons and intervention outcomes in `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` with `0600` POSIX permissions, a default 512 KiB limit (configurable via `telemetry.maxBytes`) and one rotated archive. Never writes files into `<project>/.opencode/` and never stores prompt or command text.
- **Local vs. Global Scope Isolation:** Project-local installations strictly supervise only their own project directory (and subdirectories), never interfering with unrelated workspaces sharing an OpenCode background server. Global installations supervise all opened projects while respecting per-project overrides.
- **Universal V2 Plugin Mesh Bridge (`src/bridge.ts`):** Zero-dependency N-way interoperability with **[OpenCode Hi](https://github.com/huseyincig/opencode-hi)**, **[OpenCode Smart Questions](https://github.com/huseyincig/opencode-smart-questions)**, and sibling V2 plugins via cryptographic session provenance tokens, coordinated session leases (`user_interaction`, `active_remediation`, `orchestration_dispatch`), deterministic intervention records, role capability resolution, and `opencode-mesh.state` RPC.
- **V2 Session & Fork Isolation:** Native `session.deleted`, `session.moved`, and new human prompts (including attachment-only messages) cancel stale `idleQueue` work and clear stale contracts; `session.fork` / `session.forked` are treated as independent root sessions.
- **Error Redaction:** Nested Error metadata, non-enumerable causes and aggregate errors are sanitized; executable serialization callbacks are removed and reserved JSON fields remain safe own properties.
- **Evidence-Based Task Contracts:** Analyzes human requests across 13 languages to extract required verifications (tests, builds, source reviews) and detects premature completion claims. When the host provides a tool-after observation, SHA-256 evidence is tied to the observed file contents.
- **Subagent Handoff & Background Isolation:** For synchronous `subagent` calls, Guardian owns the handoff boundary: blocking findings are remediated on the child session before the parent receives the tool result, and the parent sees the revised final child report. Background subagents (`background === true`) are isolated so they never block the parent or starve sibling background subagents.
- **Decoupled Smart Questions Coordination (`[OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1]`):** Seamlessly bridges human decisions to Smart Questions when questions or confirmations are required. Designates `auto_select=allowed` for choices and `auto_select=forbidden` for destructive actions, while preventing redundant confirmation requests.
- **14 Deterministic Rules:** Blocks shortcuts, empty stubs, unverified claims, masked errors, test weakening, leaked secrets, undeclared dependencies, and repetitive execution loops.
- **Zero Configuration:** Works instantly out of the box with production-tested defaults. Fully configurable via `opencode-guardian.json`.
- **Zero Runtime Dependencies:** Precompiled JavaScript (`dist/`) has no mandatory third-party runtime dependencies. The optional TUI utilizes the host's OpenTUI/Solid runtime.

## 📦 Installation

OpenCode Guardian supports **Global**, **Project-Local**, **Local `.opencode/plugins/` Loader / Symlink**, **Local Development (`file://`)**, and **Remote TUI Client (`cli.json`)** installation modes on OpenCode V2 (`>=2.3.0`).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> OpenCode V2 automatically discovers `./tui` and `./rpc` from `package.json` `exports` when loading `opencode-guardian` — do **not** duplicate `"opencode-guardian/tui"` in `opencode.json`.

### 1. Global Installation (All Projects — Recommended for Workstations)

To enable Guardian across **all** repositories and workspaces on your machine, add `opencode-guardian@latest` to your global OpenCode configuration file (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json`, or `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    "opencode-guardian@latest"
  ]
}
```

- **Global Behavior:** Protects every project opened in OpenCode using your global defaults (`~/.config/opencode/opencode-guardian.json`, if present) and applies any project-specific overrides found in `<project>/opencode-guardian.json` or `<project>/.opencode/opencode-guardian.json`.
- **Per-Project Opt-Out:** To disable a globally installed Guardian for one specific repository, create `<project>/opencode-guardian.json` (or `<project>/.opencode/opencode-guardian.json`) with `{ "enabled": false }`.
- **Clean Git Working Trees:** Per-project telemetry is stored externally in `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` (`0600`), so global installation never creates untracked files inside any repository's `.opencode/` folder.

### 2. Project-Local Installation (Single Repository / Team Setup)

To enable Guardian **only** for a specific repository, add `opencode-guardian@latest` to `<project>/opencode.json` (or `<project>/.opencode/opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    "opencode-guardian@latest"
  ]
}
```

- **Strict Project Scope Isolation:** When installed locally in a project, Guardian scopes all hooks, stream watchers, preflight checks, and idle inspections strictly to that project's directory (and its subdirectories). It will **never** interfere with other projects running on the same shared OpenCode background server.

### 3. `.opencode/plugins/` Local Wrapper / Symlink Installation (Monorepo & Air-Gapped)

If you manage plugins via OpenCode's `.opencode/plugins/` directory (either project-locally at `<project>/.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian` or globally at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian`) with a local or symlinked package in `.opencode/node_modules/opencode-guardian`:

1. Install or symlink the package into `.opencode/node_modules/opencode-guardian`:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p .opencode/node_modules
   ln -s /path/to/opencode-guardian .opencode/node_modules/opencode-guardian
   ```
2. Create the plugin loader wrapper in `.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian/`:
   - `.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian/package.json`:
     ```json
     {
       "name": "opencode-guardian-local",
       "private": true,
       "type": "module",
       "exports": {
         ".": "./index.ts",
         "./tui": "./tui.tsx"
       }
     }
     ```
   - `.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian/index.ts`:
     ```ts
     export { default } from "opencode-guardian";
     ```
   - `.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian/tui.tsx`:
     ```tsx
     export { default } from "opencode-guardian/tui";
     ```

### 4. Local Development (`file://` Source Checkout)

To load Guardian directly from a local git checkout (after running `npm run build`):

```json
{
  "plugin": [
    "file:///path/to/opencode-guardian"
  ]
}
```

### 5. Remote Server / Split TUI Client (`cli.json`)

For CLI-only remote-server connections where the OpenCode server runs on a remote host and your local terminal runs only the TUI client, configure `"plugin": ["opencode-guardian/tui"]` in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": [
    "opencode-guardian/tui"
  ]
}
```

### Installation Scope & State Summary

| Installation Mode | Config / Loader Location | Active Scope | Audit Log Location (`0600`) | Touches `<project>/.opencode/`? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Global** | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian` | All projects (unless disabled per-project) | `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` | **No** |
| **Project-Local** | `<project>/opencode.json`, `<project>/.opencode/opencode.json`, or `<project>/.opencode/plugins/opencode-guardian` | Strictly `<project>` (and subdirectories) | `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` | **No** |
| **Custom Override** | `OPENCODE_GUARDIAN_STATE_DIR=/custom/dir` | Active scope | `/custom/dir/guardian-events.jsonl` | **No** |

Refer to the [OpenCode V2 plugin documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/) for host loading details.

## 🖥️ TUI Sidebar Interface

OpenCode Guardian includes a dedicated V2 TUI extension (`./tui`) that mounts into OpenCode's sidebar. It displays live status, intervention counters, and update notices.

### 🔌 Enabling the TUI Sidebar

In OpenCode V2, terminal UI widgets are automatically discovered from the package's `./tui` export when `"opencode-guardian@latest"` is listed in `plugins`:

1. Add `"opencode-guardian@latest"` to `"plugins"` in your `opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`).
2. Start OpenCode as usual (`opencode`).
3. The Guardian widget appears in OpenCode's `sidebar.content` (and `session.composer.top`) slots without replacing existing sidebar sections.

### 🔽 Collapsed View (Default)

```text
▶ Guardian                 v0.16.1
Status                       ● Active
Interventions                 0w · 0r
```

- **Header:** Clickable header displaying the Guardian brand, current version, and an optional green `(↑)` update badge when a newer npm release is detected.
- **Status:** Most recent event, distinguishing verified, failed and unverified remediation as well as preflight decisions; counters reflect retained audit history.
- **Interventions:** Compact summary of warnings (`w`) and remediation requests (`r`); independent outcomes are available through `Guardian: Status`.

Clicking the `▶ Guardian` header expands the widget:

```text
▼ Guardian                 v0.16.1
Preflight                  ○ disabled
Inspected                           0
Blocked                             0
Warnings                            0
Remediations                        0
```

- **Preflight:** Current shell protection mode (`○ disabled` or `● active`).
- **Inspected / Blocked:** Real-time count of commands evaluated and prevented.
- **Blocked** counts only commands denied by active preflight; post-turn remediation requests are tracked separately.
- **Warnings / Remediations:** Detailed intervention statistics for the active project.
- **Update available:** The first row immediately below the header in both views shows the newer published version; it stays hidden when there is no update.
- **Auto-Refresh:** The widget polls the isolated project event log (`~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl`) every 2.5 seconds to reflect live metrics without reloading.
- **Hiding / Disabling:** Setting `"enabled": false` in `opencode-guardian.json` automatically unregisters and hides the TUI sidebar.

## 🔒 Privacy-Safe Audit Events

Guardian stores a structured JSONL audit in `~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl` (or `$OPENCODE_GUARDIAN_STATE_DIR/guardian-events.jsonl` when overridden) — never polluting `<project>/.opencode/`. Each entry has a timestamp, random event ID, event kind, action and outcome. Findings include only the **rule ID and a predefined reason code**, such as `masked-verification-failure`, `destructive-operation-not-authorized` or `missing-follow-up-review`. The session ID is reduced to a 16-character SHA-256 fingerprint. Custom tool names are replaced with a generic category.

```json
{"at":"2026-10-04T00:00:00.000Z","id":"123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000","kind":"post-remediation","action":"remediation-requested","outcome":"unverified","rules":["task/completion-gate"],"reasons":[{"rule":"task/completion-gate","code":"missing-follow-up-review"}]}
```

- `unverified` means an instruction was sent, **not** that the agent completed it.
- A warning uses `reported`; a preflight denial uses `prevented` only when the command was actually rejected before execution.
- No prompts, assistant responses, raw commands, file contents, finding snippets, original session IDs, credentials or secrets are written.
- The active log is bounded to 512 KiB by default (configurable up to 2 MiB via `telemetry.maxBytes` or `OPENCODE_GUARDIAN_MAX_LOG_BYTES`), with one rotated archive (`guardian-events.jsonl.1`). In default `violations` mode, high-frequency benign events bypass disk writes completely.
- To inspect the exact log path and counters for a project, run `opencode-guardian-status /path/to/project`.

## 📋 The 14 Guardrail Rules

OpenCode Guardian evaluates assistant turns against 14 deterministic rules. Rules can be configured as `error`, `warn`, or `off`; remediation is bounded and post-turn findings cannot undo an already-executed command:

| Category | Rule ID | Default | What It Enforces |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Discipline** | `discipline/no-evasion` | `error` | Blocks unsupported dismissals such as claiming a test failure is "pre-existing" or "out of scope" unless verified by baseline checks. |
| **Discipline** | `discipline/no-apology` | `error` | Blocks sycophantic, defensive, or repetitive apology language across multiple languages. |
| **Quality** | `quality/no-shortcuts` | `error` | Blocks concrete deferred-work phrases (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, "will do later"). Ambiguous hedging phrases are flagged as advisory warnings. |
| **Integrity** | `integrity/no-stubs` | `error` | Blocks `NotImplementedError`, empty function stubs, Rust `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()`, and placeholder returns. |
| **Integrity** | `integrity/no-unverified-claims` | `error` | Correlates success claims with observed outcomes and explicit current passed-test counts with fresh supported summaries. Direct contradictions block. |
| **Integrity** | `integrity/no-silent-failure` | `error` | Blocks test, build, lint, typecheck, or audit commands masked with `\|\| true`, `exit 0`, or suppressed exit codes. |
| **Safety** | `safety/no-truncation` | `error` | Blocks source edit placeholders; observed whole-file definition loss produces an advisory. Literal examples and documentation are excluded from placeholder checks. |
| **Safety** | `safety/destructive-operations` | `warn` | Inspects hard resets, force pushes, recursive deletion (`rm -rf`), database drops, and unpublish actions. Plain `rm` requires explicit scoped user consent. |
| **Testing** | `testing/no-cheat` | `error` | Blocks malicious test tampering: targeted `describe.skip`, `it.skip`, `test.skip`, `fit`, or assertion stripping in test files. |
| **Security** | `security/no-secrets` | `error` | Blocks hardcoded API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, JWTs, private keys, database URLs with passwords). |
| **Manifest** | `manifest/no-ghost-deps` | `error` | Blocks undeclared third-party imports. Runtime JS/TS imports declared only in dev dependencies are advisory unless `productionOnly` is enabled; type-only/test/build imports retain exceptions. |
| **Runtime** | `runtime/circuit-breaker` | `error` | Blocks identical execution failures repeated 3 times without progress and detects degenerative token/phrase cycles in reasoning and text. Stream watcher aborts runaway generation in-flight. |
| **Task** | `task/instruction-fidelity` | `error` | Checks narrow English/Turkish research-only constraints against observed actions and prevents historical refusals or redundant confirmation handoffs from overriding current instructions. |
| **Task** | `task/completion-gate` | `error` | Requires observed requested verification. Recognized zero-test, skipped-only and conflicting summaries cannot satisfy a required test run. |

## ⚙️ Configuration (`opencode-guardian.json`)

Guardian works out of the box with zero configuration. You can customize rules and thresholds by placing `opencode-guardian.json` in your project root, `.opencode/`, or `~/.config/opencode/`:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "remediationBudget": 1,
  "iterationBudget": 3,
  "updateNotice": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "preflight": {
    "enabled": false
  },
  "telemetry": {
    "enabled": true,
    "level": "violations",
    "maxBytes": 524288
  },
  "rules": {
    "discipline/no-evasion": "error",
    "discipline/no-apology": "error",
    "quality/no-shortcuts": {
      "severity": "error",
      "customPhrases": ["not my job", "out of scope for me"],
      "exceptions": ["tempdir", "temporaryfile"]
    },
    "integrity/no-stubs": "error",
    "integrity/no-unverified-claims": "error",
    "integrity/no-silent-failure": "error",
    "safety/no-truncation": "error",
    "safety/destructive-operations": "warn",
    "testing/no-cheat": "error",
    "security/no-secrets": "error",
    "manifest/no-ghost-deps": "error",
    "runtime/circuit-breaker": "error",
    "task/instruction-fidelity": "error",
    "task/completion-gate": "error"
  }
}
```

### 🎛️ Severity Options:
- `"error"`: High-confidence violation triggers an automatic remediation prompt (bounded by `remediationBudget`).
- `"warn"`: Recorded in telemetry and displayed in TUI, but does not interrupt agent flow.
- `"off"`: Completely disables the rule.

### 📈 Telemetry & Audit Log Options:
- `telemetry.level`:
  - `"violations"`: (Default) Logs only security violations, preflight blocks, warnings, and remediation actions. Bypasses clean turns and benign commands (`preflight-allowed`, `post-inspected`), reducing disk I/O by 90–95%.
  - `"all"`: Logs all events including benign command executions and clean turn evaluations.
  - `"off"`: Disables all file writes (zero I/O), ideal for headless CI/CD runs.

The diagram illustrates the **v0.16.1** pure OpenCode V2 (`>=2.3.0`) runtime, wired via `setup(ctx)` hooks (`session.hook("prompt")`, `session.hook("context")`, `session.hook("experimental.idle")`, `tool.hook("execute.before")`, `tool.hook("execute.after")`, `shell.hook("create.before")`, `stream.hook`, `event.subscribe`), typed `./rpc` intervention endpoints (`opencode-guardian/rpc`), `opencode-mesh.state` RPC (`src/bridge.ts`), and `session.fork` / `session.forked` root-session isolation. Strict preflight is **opt-in** and evaluates recognized or configured tools and shell creations; an out-of-scope tool is still governed by host permissions. Tool-after observations and SHA-256 file snapshots are captured **when the host supplies supported evidence**. Supported whole-file writes also use before/after observations for advisory content-loss detection; missing before hooks cannot reconstruct old file content. For delegated `subagent` work, Guardian preserves capability-aware remediation isolation: synchronous write-capable subagents retain bounded remediation before parent release, read-only subagents avoid synthetic remediation loops, background subagents (`background === true`) are isolated from the foreground handoff barrier so sibling background subagents are never starved, and per-rule fingerprints distinguish substantive errors. Teardown remains idempotent across `AbortController` signals and LIFO hook rollback; background polling/cleanup intervals call `.unref?.()`, while active one-shot coalesce and retry timers keep the event loop alive until completion or abort.

## 🤝 Smart Questions Coordination Protocol

> [!NOTE]
> Guardian and Smart Questions are **completely standalone plugins** that operate independently with zero required package dependencies. When installed together in the same OpenCode environment, they optionally coordinate through this decoupled, versioned protocol (`[OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1]`).

OpenCode Guardian coordinates with **[OpenCode Smart Questions](https://github.com/huseyincig/opencode-smart-questions)** through an independent, versioned protocol block (`[OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1]`) without requiring direct package dependencies:

```text
[opencode-guardian remediation]

[OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1]
source=guardian
action=question_required
kind=choice
auto_select=allowed
handoff_id=gq_c47f9a12b0

Please ask the user which deployment strategy is preferred.
```

### Deterministic Handoff Architecture:

- **Legitimate Choices (`kind=choice / auto_select=allowed`):** When technical decisions legitimately require user selection (e.g. strategy choices, architecture alternatives), Guardian emits a choice handoff. Smart Questions presents native forms with recommended options and auto-selects after a safe countdown if uninterrupted.
- **Destructive Confirmations (`kind=approval / auto_select=forbidden`):** Irreversible or high-risk actions (e.g. database drops, production deletions) emit an approval handoff with `auto_select=forbidden`. Smart Questions strictly suppresses auto-reply and countdown, requiring mandatory human confirmation.
- **Redundant Question Prevention:** When the user already gave explicit direction (governed by `task/instruction-fidelity`), Guardian blocks unnecessary confirmation questions and withholds handoffs entirely.
- **Host Provenance & Anti-Spoofing:** All handoffs require trusted Guardian provenance metadata (`metadata["opencode-guardian"] === true`). Unauthenticated user prompt text cannot forge handoffs.
- **TTL & Turn Binding:** Active handoffs expire after 120 seconds, reset cleanly on new human turns, and cannot be reused after consumption.

    participant U as User / Agent
    participant G as Guardian
    participant SQ as Smart Questions
    participant Host as OpenCode Host

    U->>G: Agent turn evaluates blocking rule

        G->>Host: Remediation + [OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1] (auto_select=allowed)
        Host->>SQ: Trusted handoff received
        U->>Host: Native question with [SQ:recommended]
        SQ->>Host: Countdown & auto-selects recommended option
    else Destructive / Sensitive Action
        G->>Host: Remediation + [OPENCODE_HANDOFF:v1] (auto_select=forbidden)
        Host->>SQ: Trusted approval handoff received
        U->>Host: Native question with choices
        Note over SQ,Host: Auto-reply strictly disabled - user must click manually
    else Work Already Authorized
        G->>Host: Instruction fidelity blocks - no handoff generated
        U->>Host: Agent directly continues authorized work
    end

## 🔬 Scientific Foundation & Academic Research

OpenCode Guardian's architecture and security models are grounded in peer-reviewed computer science literature and industry security frameworks:

1. **"Guardians of the Agents" (Erik Meijer, Communications of the ACM, Dec 2025):**
   - In [*Guardians of the Agents*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3777544) (*Communications of the ACM*, DOI: [`10.1145/3777544`](https://doi.org/10.1145/3777544)), Erik Meijer formalized the paradigm of using independent, host-level supervisory software ("Guardians") that monitor and enforce behavioral invariants over autonomous AI agents before and after tool execution, without requiring prompt-level instructions or modifying model weights.
   - OpenCode Guardian directly realizes this paradigm through its pure OpenCode V2 engine, evaluating preflight invariants before execution and correlating multi-step evidence at `session.idle`.

2. **The GuardFall Vulnerability Research (Adversa AI, June 2026):**
   - Discovered by Adversa AI in June 2026, the *GuardFall* research revealed systemic flaws across 10 out of 11 popular coding agents where string-matching blocklists failed to detect obfuscated shell commands (such as quote removal `r''m`, variable expansion `$IFS`, paired backtick substitution, and encoded Base64 pipelines).
   - OpenCode Guardian incorporates dedicated conservative shell-pattern analysis ([`src/shell-risk.ts`](src/shell-risk.ts)) and regression suites ([`tests/guardfall-regression.test.mjs`](tests/guardfall-regression.test.mjs)) to recognize documented GuardFall-style patterns during post-turn inspection and opt-in strict preflight.

3. **OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026):**
   - OpenCode Guardian is architected to address critical vulnerabilities defined in the OWASP Agentic Top 10 framework, including **ASI01** (Agent Goal Hijacking), **ASI02** (Tool Misuse), **ASI03** (Identity & Privilege Abuse), **ASI05** (Unexpected Code Execution), and **ASI08** (Cascading Failures).
   - Detailed mapping and capability boundaries are documented in [`docs/owasp-agentic-top10-2026.md`](docs/owasp-agentic-top10-2026.md).

# Engine discipline coverage and evidence boundaries

Guardian v0.16.1 targets pure OpenCode V2 (`>=2.3.0`, verified through `v2.3.2`). It keeps the existing fourteen rule IDs and remediation budgets, adds the typed `./rpc` export, `shell.hook("create.before")` preflight, Universal V2 Plugin Mesh Bridge (`src/bridge.ts`), and external per-project state isolation, and adds no runtime dependencies or installed skills. (OpenCode V1 support ended in `v0.14.0`.)

## Evidence

`EvidenceRecord` now carries `testSummary`, `outcomeReason` and observed `editIntegrity`. The original host exit code is preserved, with normalization for standardized `"Exit code: N"` outputs and explicit signal kill/timeout errors (`SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`, `SIGINT`). Only assistant tool parts produce evidence; prose, user examples and system text do not.

Supported complete aggregate summaries: Node TAP/spec, pytest, Jest and Vitest. Counts are bounded and must reconcile. Known pytest warning/deselection fields are ignored rather than counted as executed tests. Unknown formats retain the host outcome without inventing counts. Missing exit codes, masked pipelines and ambiguous compound commands retain the existing conservative handling.

- Zero-test and skipped-only runs cannot satisfy required verification.
- Failed host execution cannot be promoted by a passing summary.
- A failing summary paired with exit zero is ambiguous, not successful verification.
- Host cancellation metadata or narrow explicit user-cancellation evidence is distinct from an execution failure. Pytest exit 2 alone is **not** proof of user cancellation; collection errors use it too.
- Explicit English passed-test count claims are compared with fresh observed totals; historical and uncertain statements are excluded.

The output parser supports selected observed formats, not all runner versions. Node itself recommends test stream events for programmatic consumers; Guardian does not silently replace users' runners or force a reporter. A green exit without recognized counts preserves legacy verification behavior, not a claim that every test was discovered.

## Rule coverage

| Rule | Improvement or preserved guarantee | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `discipline/no-evasion` | File-specific baseline claims need matching comparison targets. | Generic baseline compatibility remains; reading source alone is not proof that a failing test existed previously. |
| `discipline/no-apology` | Explicit project-configured exceptions apply only to their matching span. | No universal semantic sycophancy detector; useful uncertainty and factual correction remain valid. |
| `quality/no-shortcuts` | Existing scoped placeholder authorization and phrase exceptions have legitimate-negative coverage. | No new broad style bans or inferred documentation requirements. |
| `integrity/no-stubs` | Quoted examples are masked; actual empty named JS/TS implementations are detected. | Lexical analysis, not a complete AST; intentional callbacks/constructors, fixture paths and declarations have exemptions. Complex return types remain conservative. |
| `integrity/no-unverified-claims` | Fresh observed passed counts support or contradict explicit current count claims. | Unsupported output formats and unavailable facts do not manufacture verification. |
| `integrity/no-silent-failure` | Literal examples are excluded; constant error fallbacks are advisory; hidden verification substitutions are inspected. | Static shell subset; an intentional recovery is not automatically a failure. |
| `safety/no-truncation` | Before/after whole-file observations detect suspicious definition loss. Strict file preflight rejects source placeholders. | Content-loss findings are advisory; missing observations are not reconstructed from current disk. No rollback. |
| `safety/destructive-operations` | Hook bypasses require explicit authorization; literal repositories, push refspecs and reset targets remain scoped. | Static shell subset; existing strict preflight is still opt-in and host permissions remain necessary. |
| `testing/no-cheat` | Quoted examples are inert; conditional assertions are advisory. | Assertion quality cannot be proven from syntax alone; legitimate test edits keep existing scoped authorization. |
| `security/no-secrets` | File-write and output checks share known credential formats, including GitHub variants and JWTs. | No entropy-only hard block, external credential verification or new network requests. |

Live text/reasoning checks honor `error`, `warn`, and `off`, in string or object form. | Repetition detection is heuristic: intentional repetition can trigger it. The bounded window supports periods up to 512 UTF-16 code units and excludes short quoted numeric/hex fixtures. A stop request is not proof of interruption or token savings. Rejected stop calls retry on later growth at most three times; an ambiguous timeout suppresses overlapping retries. V2 cannot cancel an already issued host call. |
| `task/instruction-fidelity` | Narrow English/Turkish research-only constraints are checked against observed mutations, installs and pushes. | Post-turn detection cannot undo a completed write. Other phrasings/languages are not claimed as universally understood. |
| `task/completion-gate` | Required zero-test/skipped-only/conflicting runs do not count as passing. Subagents reporting in-progress turns or intermediate updates without claiming completion are protected from false-positive completion gate blocking. | No automatic assertion that source inspection covered an entire repository. |

## Edit observations and safety

V2 before/after hooks capture hashes, sizes and declaration-name sets for recognized whole-file `content` writes via `VerificationSnapshotStore` (preserving both `editIntegrity` and `fingerprint` on the same `callID`). Files must resolve inside the project, be regular files and not exceed 2 MiB. A file with more than 1,024 distinct declaration names is outside this bounded observation. Pending before observations are capped at 32 per session and completed records at 512; session cleanup clears them. Raw source content is not retained in audit events.

An advisory is produced when an observed successful replacement removes at least two declaration names and reduces byte length below half. These are explicit heuristics for review, **not proof of unintended deletion**. Targeted edits, missing before hooks, failed writes and unsupported mutation shapes do not invent a previous file. Empty successful replacements still count as mutations and invalidate prior verification.

Code lexical views are limited to 2 MiB and 32 nested template expressions. Supported JS/TS paths retain private fields and executable template interpolations. Other syntax and general shell interpretation are not guaranteed. An intentionally quoted natural-language deletion target may conservatively require clearer authorization; quoted examples never grant permission.

## Configuration

Default production-dependency findings are advisory, including when the rule severity is `error`, because a build step may bundle the import. Opt in to strict production dependency checks with:

    "manifest/no-ghost-deps": {

      "productionOnly": true

`blockEmptyHandlers` continues to control empty-handler blocking. Constant fallback and conditional-assertion findings stay advisory. Prose exceptions are literal phrases supplied through trusted project configuration, not authorization granted by comments in inspected code. No defaults enable a new external scanner or network service.

# Task Contract and OpenCode V2 Adapter Architecture

Documentation for OpenCode Guardian **v0.16.1**.

Guardian implements a pure **OpenCode V2** (`@opencode/plugin >=2.3.0`) architecture across its server entry (`.`), terminal UI entry (`./tui`), and typed intervention RPC contract (`./rpc`) using standard, non-invasive V2 plugin hooks.

## Task Contract Lifecycle

A new human prompt via `ctx.session.hook("prompt", ...)` cancels any in-flight `idleQueue` inspection and clears stale `TaskContract` guidance before extracting the new text contract. Attachment-only or empty prompts also end the prior task. Native `session.deleted` clears cached capabilities, contracts, and pending idle work; cancelled capability queries cannot revive a deleted session's cache. These paths have dedicated [debugging regressions](../tests/debug-regressions.test.mjs) and [V2 Stage 2a regressions](../tests/v2-stage2a-regressions.test.mjs).

1. **Extraction on Human Turn:**
   - Filters out synthetic prompts and previous remediation cycles.
   - Identifies actionable requests, repeated review loops, source verification obligations, and individual verification commands (`test`, `build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `audit`).
2. **Context Guidance:**
   - Injects structured guidance via `ctx.session.hook("context", ...)` before the model turn, preventing the agent from prioritizing earlier deferrals or hallucinating completion.
   - Normalizes V2 `shell` and `agent-switched` context entries alongside standard message parts.
3. **Evidence Collection after `session.idle`:**
   - Normalizes recorded tool invocations through `collectTurnEvidence` into shared evidence records, including V2 `Error` instances and `{ type, message }` tool error objects.
   - Supported complete Node/pytest/Jest/Vitest summaries add reconciled counts and outcome reasons. Unknown formats do not invent counts; host failures cannot become success because output prints a passing summary.
   - Validates chronological order: verifications run *before* the latest file edit are marked stale.
   - Substantive source inspections (file reads, line-bearing search/diff matches) are distinguished from superficial filename listings. Note that observable inspection of modified files confirms post-change re-inspection but cannot prove exhaustive whole-repository coverage (`reviewProvesFullCoverage: false`).
4. **Completion Evaluation:**
   - If an explicit iterative review task terminates without observing the required post-change verification, an automated remediation is triggered.
   - An `"in progress"` reply with a mutation does not falsely mark `task/completion-gate` as `"remediation-verified"`.
   - A required test run cannot be satisfied by a recognized zero-test, skipped-only or conflicting summary.
   - Continues up to `iterationBudget` (default `3`, max `5`), requiring observable progress on each turn.
5. **Circuit Breaking:**
   - Detects explicit blockers (unmet dependencies, missing credentials, system errors) and halts automatic retry loops to present a transparent report to the user.
   - Explicit user cancellation is distinguished from repeated execution failures. Pytest exit 2 alone is not cancellation evidence because collection errors also use it.
6. **Foreground & Background Subagent Coordination:**
   - Synchronous V2 `subagent` calls (`background !== true`) are tracked from `execute.before` to `execute.after`.
   - If the child session has blocking Guardian findings, the parent-facing tool result is held while Guardian sends bounded remediation to the child and waits for that turn to finish.
   - The child is re-inspected before release. When remediation produces a revised final report, that report replaces the stale first-pass child output returned to the parent.
   - Background subagents (`background === true`) do not enter the blocking handoff path and are isolated so they neither starve sibling background subagents nor block the parent turn.
   - Forked sessions (`session.fork` / `session.forked`) are treated as independent root sessions.

## Evidence, Standardized Shell Output, and Telemetry Boundaries

Evidence normalization in `src/evidence.ts` recognizes standardized `"Exit code: N"` outputs and tracks explicit signal kill or timeout errors (`SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`, `SIGINT`) as well as V2 `Error` and `{ type, message }` error shapes. Read-only Git inspection tools (`diff`, `git_diff`, `log`, `git_log`, `show`, `git_show`) are recognized without triggering destructive warnings.

The Low-I/O Telemetry architecture (`src/telemetry.ts`) provides `telemetry.level` (`"violations" | "all" | "off"`, default: `"violations"`), filtering out high-frequency benign events (`preflight-allowed`, `post-inspected`) to eliminate 90–95% of disk I/O and prevent test and benchmark freezes. Verified state directory permissions are re-verified via `lstatSync` and cached in-memory, `telemetryConfigRegistry` is cleaned up on early setup errors, and event logs are strictly bounded to 512 KiB by default (configurable via `telemetry.maxBytes`). Supported whole-file writes carry before/after hashes, sizes, and declaration-name loss into idle inspection via `VerificationSnapshotStore`. See [edit observation limits](discipline-coverage.md#edit-observations-and-safety) for project confinement and memory bounds.

Research-only enforcement recognizes narrow English/Turkish phrases and checks observed writes, installs and pushes after the turn. It does not cover every language supported by task-contract extraction and cannot undo a completed mutation. File-specific baseline claims need matching comparison targets; quoted examples cannot grant destructive-operation permission.

## Error Handling & Resiliency

- **Graceful Fallbacks:** Missing optional hooks in transition environments fail open without breaking the core inspection pipeline. `resolveV2AgentCapability` safely handles array, `{ data }`, and null/throwing list responses.
- **Fail-Fast Security:** When strict preflight (`preflight.enabled: true`) is explicitly configured, setup requires valid tool/shell hook registration and rolls back any earlier hooks if a later registration fails.
- **Configuration Integrity:** Explicit configuration files (`opencode-guardian.json`, `.opencode/opencode-guardian.json`) must be valid JSON objects. Corrupt or malformed files throw a visible `GuardianConfigError` rather than silently degrading to insecure defaults.
- **Bounded Session State & Timers:** Per-session Maps/Sets and capability caches are bounded and evicted on `session.deleted` or teardown; periodic background cleanup/polling intervals call `.unref?.()`, while active one-shot coalesce and retry timers keep the event loop alive until completion or abort.

---

## V2 Instance, Session Scope, and RPC Surface

V2 `ctx.location.directory` identifies the plugin instance; it is not guaranteed to be the working directory of every session. Guardian resolves top-level `location.directory` first, then `ctx.session.get({ sessionID }).location.directory` when available, falling back to `event.cwd` (on `shell.hook("create.before")`) or the instance directory. Tool-before and `shell.hook("create.before")` checks use the known session/cwd directory or fall back to the instance directory. Hook registration and fail-fast strict-preflight availability checks happen at instance setup; another project's configuration cannot supply a missing host hook. Use independent plugin instances for projects requiring different strict policies.

When an event subscription unexpectedly ends or fails, Guardian records an inspection error and makes up to three bounded stream attempts. Teardown aborts pending reconnects. Failure to restore the stream is logged visibly; this is not a substitute for monitoring host health.

The typed `./rpc` export (`src/intervention-rpc.ts`) exposes `guardian.interventions.get` and `guardian.interventions.clear` using `Rpc.define` (`@opencode/plugin/rpc`):
- `sessionID` inputs enforce `maxLength: 256`.
- `guardian.interventions.clear` with `{}` is strictly scoped to the requested project `directory` / `location.directory` (falling back to the plugin instance's `directory` and resolving uncached session directories asynchronously), preventing cross-project intervention clearing.
- In `src/tui.tsx`, per-session generation/epoch tracking prevents in-flight 500ms RPC polls from resurrecting interventions cleared by `/guardian-reset`, clean turns, `session.moved`, or `session.deleted`.

---

## Strict Command Resolution and Example Credentials

Multi-stage shell commands are split via `splitShellStages` so preflight inspects every stage for destructive operations, hallucinated or typosquatted package installs, and lazy commit messages in both `tool.execute.before` and `shell.create.before`.

Literal backtick substitutions that construct a destructive executable name are classified before execution. Unknown executable names generated through dynamic substitution are denied in strict preflight. Passive documentation examples and echo output remain permitted. Standard MCP shell-tool IDs (such as `mcp__provider__shell_exec`), scoped Git operations, and common literal `mkfs`/fork-bomb signatures are also recognized. The shell-pattern detector is not a full shell interpreter.

All example and template files remain subject to secret scanning. A narrowly defined local database example password is tolerated only in an example file and only on localhost or a reserved example host. Real-looking API tokens, strong passwords, and remote credentials are never exempted by filename. `sanitizeObject` and `sanitizeMessages` preserve `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` buffers and non-plain object prototypes (`Message` class).

---

## Guardian TUI, Commands, and Handoff Lifecycle

`src/tui.tsx` targets pure OpenCode V2 (`setup(ctx)`) and exports an adaptive `dist/tui.js` entry that safely falls back to `./tui-standalone.js` in standalone Bun or Node runtimes without crashing on `opentui:runtime-module` resolution.

Both server and TUI share SDK-independent, redacted reporting in `src/commands.ts`. TUI registers 7 `/guardian-*` palette/slash commands plus the `/guardian` dispatcher and a global keymap layer alongside the additive `sidebar.content` and `session.composer.top` slots. Minimal TUI contexts without optional `data`/`command` APIs fail safe without throwing.

`/guardian-reset` requires confirmation and appends a `statistics-reset` event. Counters restart while security history remains subject to normal bounded rotation; protection and configuration are unchanged.

## v0.13.0 Streaming Loop Hardening & Degenerative Cycle Breaker

- **Language-Agnostic Degenerative Cycle Detection:** Implemented `detectDegenerativeLoop` in `src/degeneration.ts` to detect repetitive token cascades and collapse states in assistant text and reasoning (including DeepSeek V4.1 Flash *"Hmm..."*, Kimi 2.7 Chinese/Japanese ideogram cascades, runaway punctuation, and code token repeats like *"None, None, None..."*).
- **Post-Turn Circuit Breaker Integration:** Enhanced `runtime/circuit-breaker` to inspect assistant text and reasoning parts in `currentTurn`, producing structured findings and targeted remediation prompts instructing the model to clear stalled thoughts and proceed without repetition.
- **Live In-Flight Streaming Inspection:** V1 inspects `message.part.updated` only for the active assistant message; V2 consumes native `session.text.delta` and `session.reasoning.delta` events. Inspection uses a bounded 2,048 UTF-16 code-unit tail and checks after at least 40 new code units following the initial inspection. `error` requests `client.session.abort` (V1) or `context.session.interrupt({ sessionID, resume: false })` (V2); `warn` records a warning and `off` disables intervention, including object-form settings. V2 event ingestion continues while project lookup and interruption are pending, allowing completion, deletion, moves, and newer responses to invalidate stale detections. Failed calls are recorded and explicitly rejected requests may retry on subsequent growth, at most three times per response. A three-second timeout records an error and suppresses overlapping stop retries; the V2 host API cannot cancel an already issued call. Disposal cancels inspection and discards late results. A successful API response is logged as `stream-interrupt-requested` with an unverified outcome, without claiming prevention, saved tokens, or delivery of a remediation prompt.
- **Negative False-Positive Protections:** Excluded Markdown table rows, comment banners, horizontal rules, small fixture arrays, standard code loops, and quoted numeric/hex literals of 15–128 characters, including incomplete streaming prefixes. Periodic patterns up to 512 code units are supported within the bounded window. The character-diversity fallback is a heuristic, not a Shannon entropy or compression calculation. Intentional long repetition can still trigger the heuristic; this is not a universal decoding-collapse guarantee.
- **Regression Suite:** The 24 cases in `tests/degenerative-loops.test.mjs` cover multilingual positives, negatives, post-turn rules, and adapter integration; `tests/stream-loop-hardening.test.mjs` adds lifecycle, settings, rejected requests, concurrency, project isolation, literal fixtures, and long-period regressions. These use mocked host contracts; real-host acceptance was not rerun.
- **Measured Detector Cost (2026-10-23):** Node v24.22.0, 1,000 warm-up checks followed by 4,000 checks per input, using the default 2,048-code-unit window. Long English cycles: median 0.0060 ms / p95 0.0077 ms; CJK cycles: 0.0072 / 0.0081 ms; nonperiodic source code: 0.1854 / 0.2236 ms. These local measurements cover the detector only; they do not establish a universal latency or zero-overhead guarantee.

## Methodological Boundaries & Limitations

1. **Opt-In Preflight:** Strict preflight is an opt-in safety net (`preflight.enabled: true`) designed to catch common accidental destructive commands and obvious secrets before execution. It is pattern-based and does not replace operating system user permissions, containers, or sandboxing.
2. **Post-Turn Scope:** Post-turn rule violations guide agent behavior and trigger automated remediation, but cannot retroactively reverse an operation that already completed.
3. **Log Rotation & Low-I/O Telemetry:** The per-project event log (`~/.local/state/opencode-guardian/projects/<projectHash>/guardian-events.jsonl`) is bounded by default to 512 KiB (configurable via `telemetry.maxBytes` or `OPENCODE_GUARDIAN_MAX_LOG_BYTES`), with one rotated archive (`guardian-events.jsonl.1`). In default `violations` mode, benign preflight-allowed and clean-turn events bypass disk I/O entirely, eliminating excessive disk churn without creating files inside `<project>/.opencode/`.
